name: City Council Regular Meeting of August 2, 2022

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF AUGUST 2, 2022

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Alma D. Puente, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Martin R. Herrera, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Dr. Maria Morales, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  m) Mayor Pro Tem Puente
  s) Mayor Ancona  5-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various legislative bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council will attempt to address and complete all
  Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m. If the City Council completes
  all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the City Council will take a short recess
  and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m. In the event the City
  Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed Session items by 7:00
  p.m., the City Council will hear all such remaining items toward the end of the meeting,
  immediately following Council Communications. Should any member of the public wish to
  address the City Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the City Council shall
  allow such person to address the City Council on such matter(s) prior to going into Closed
  Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an agendized Closed
  Session matter shall (i) call-in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed on page
  1 of this agenda, above, prior to the City Council going into closed session; and (ii) be
  subject to a single speaker time allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total per
  speaker to address the City Council on any or all closed session items of business.

  Mayor Ancona invited members of the public to address the City Council on Closed
  Session Items 4.1 through 4.3.

  Armando Herman – Spoke about closed session items.

  Mike Greenspan – Spoke about closed session items.

  Mayor Ancona and the City Council recessed into Closed Session at approximately
  6:10 p.m. Mayor Ancona and the City Council reconvened from Closed Session at
  approximately 7:23 p.m.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla reported out of Closed Session with respect
  to Items 4.1 through 4.3.
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 2, 2022

  4.1  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(2) – Conference with Legal Counsel to Discuss Facts and
  Circumstances Which May Create Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Update provided by staff and legal counsel, direction given by the City
  Council, but not final action taken.

  4.2  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(2) and
  54956.9(e)(2) – Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation/Significant
  Exposure to Litigation – One (1) Matter.

  Update provided by staff and legal counsel, direction given by the City
  Council, but not final action taken.

  4.3  Closed Session Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6 – Conference with
  Labor Negotiators.

  Bargaining Units Subject to Negotiations: El Monte General Unit (SEIU Local
  721); El Monte General Mid-Management Unit (SEIU Local 721); El Monte Police
  Officers Association; El Monte Police Mid-Manager’s Association; and All
  Unrepresented Employees of City Executive Team.

  City’s Designated Negotiator: Alma K. Martinez, City Manager and John Nguyen,

  Update provided by staff and legal counsel, direction given by the City
  Council, but not final action taken.

  OPEN SESSION PROCEEDINGS

(Commencing at 7:00 p.m. or as soon thereafter as the City Council reconvene from Closed
Session/Short Recess).

5.  INVOCATION:  Chaplain Manny Coronilla, Calvary Chapel El Monte.
  Chaplain Esrom Lempao, Non-Denominational.

6.  FLAG SALUTE:  City Council. Mayor Ancona.

7.  RECOGNITIONS, HONORS AND COMMUNITY INTEREST PRESENTATIONS:

  7.1  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming the Week of August 7th – 13th, 2022
  “National Farmers Market Week,” and August 11, 2022 as “Farmers Market Day”
  in the City of El Monte.

  7.2  Presentation by the City Council Proclaiming September 16, 2022 as National
  Stepfamily Day.

8.  GENERAL PUBLIC COMMENT:

  This time has been set aside for members of the public to directly address the City Council
  on agendized items of business (other than those agendized as public hearing or closed
  session items) or on any other matter of interest to the speaker/caller that is within the
  subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing Authority, the Financing
  Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”). Each speaker/caller will
  be limited to a single allotment of three (3) continuous minutes total to address the Council
  on any or all matters covered by this section. As explained more specifically under the
  Public Hearing portion of this agenda, members of the public wishing to offer comment on
  items of business agendized under the Public Hearing portion of the agenda shall have a
  separate allotment of three (3) continuous minutes per speaker per public hearing item.
  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),

  2
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 2, 2022

  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for consideration
  at a future meeting. Persons wishing to address the Council on matters covered under
  General Public Comment shall call in or submit a speaker card in the manner prescribed
  on page 1 of this agenda, above, by or before the General Public Comment portion of the
  agenda is closed. The City Council shall be under no obligation to entertain comments
  from speakers/callers who submit cards or call in to speak on matters covered by the
  section after the General Public Comment portion of the agenda is closed.

  Charles Hoffman – Addressed the flag being displayed on the dais.

  Cosme Jimenez – Spoke about public records requests that he has submitted to the City.

  Armando Herman – Spoke about items on the agenda.

  Mike Greenspan – Spoke about Foothill Transit.

  Andre Quintero – Spoke about people who have been coming to the meetings who show
  no respect or regard for the City Council.

  Rodolfo Barragan – Spoke about the City Attorney’s Office.

  Gabriel Ramirez – Spoke about a flyer from 2020 that was handed out during the election
  campaign.

  Julio Ramirez – Spoke about the M Motel on Baldwin, when will this project be completed.
  Spoke about the barriers on the sidewalks.

  Ron Danison – Spoke about Item 14.6 the TOT Tax. Spoke about hiring more police
  officers. Thanked the Council for all their work.

  Jane Flores – Spoke about the fees charged by the City Attorney’s Office.

  Edward Salcedo – Spoke about a potential housing project at Kranz that he heard about.
  Spoke about the old Sargent Fletcher site.

  Written Comments –

  Sara Robles – Tired of seeing the crime rate increase in the City.

  Alicia Lara – Tired of too many car accidents in the City.

14.6  Consideration and Approval of a Resolution Calling for the Submission to El Monte
  Voters at the November 8, 2022 General Municipal Election of a Measure to
  Approve an Ordinance Increasing El Monte’s Transient Occupancy (Hotel/Motel)
  Tax Rate from 10% to 14% and Concurrent Approval for First Reading of Said
  Ordinance

  RECOMMENDATION OF BUSINESS ITEM UNDER CONSIDERATION:

  It is recommended that the City Council:

  1. By no less than 2/3 vote of all the members of the City Council (i.e., no less
  than 4 “Yes” votes), approve the attached Resolution calling for submission to
  El Monte voters at the November 8, 2022 General Municipal Election of a
  measure to approve an ordinance that increases El Monte’s transient
  occupancy (hotel/motel guest) tax rate to 14% of room rents and concurrent
  first reading of said ordinance;
  2. Authorize the City Clerk Office to coordinate with the Los Angeles County
  Registrar-Recorder’s Office and the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors
  to arrange for the inclusion of the ballot measure in the City’s November 8,
  2022 General Municipal Election ballot; and
  3. Act to decide whether the City Council or some other grouping of persons will
  prepare a ballot argument in favor of the measure and make related decisions
  as to the authorship of the argument.

18.  COUNCIL COMMUNICATIONS/REPORTS:

  18A.  Mayor Ancona

  18A.1 Discussion and Direction on Eliminating OMLO Pass Through Billing and
  Payments.

  Mayor Ancona – Looking at opportunities to eliminate pass through billing where
  possible.

  City Attorney – Can provide a report of what firms are used and the cost.

  Assistant City Attorney Richard Padilla – Can provide a monthly report.

  Mayor Pro Tem Puente – Want to make sure that this doesn’t waive the attorney
  client privilege.

  City Attorney – The information provided to the City Council in this report will not
  jeopardize this information.

  18A.2 Discussion and Direction to Provide Information and Outreach to Increase
  Safety Measures for El Monte Business Owners.

  Mayor Ancona – Would like to ask that staff work on a best practice handout to
  outreach to the businesses to prevent break-ins.

  Chief of Police Lowry provided an update on what the Police Department has been
  doing and its meeting with DEMBA after the smash and grab incident. Also
  recommended a Saturday Police Department event to bring awareness regarding
  this.

  Councilmember Martinez wanted to add doing PSAs on YouTube. The business
  license renewals will be going out soon and an invitation can be included in this
  mailout.

  9
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 2, 2022

  18A.3 Discussion on Recognition of El Monte/South El Monte Chamber of
  Commerce 100th Anniversary.

  Mayor would like to recognize the El Monte/South El Monte Chamber of
  Commerce at the Community Award Night that will take place in September.

  18A.4 Update on Community Clean Up Events.

  Maybe the City can have quarterly events staff to bring back some dates at a later
  date.
  18A.5 Update and Discussion on Campaign Ethics Presentation.

  18A.6 Update on Flock Camera Program.

  The Police Department is waiting for two additional bids to be able to purchase 17
  fixed cameras throughout the City and having two flexible cameras. Asset
  forfeiture funds can be used for this item.

  Mayor Ancona spoke about the ride-along she was on and how busy it was that
  night. Wanted to commend the Police Officers.

18B.  Mayor Pro Tem Puente

18C.  Councilman Herrera

  18C.1 Discussion and Possible Direction on Aligning the Membership of the City’s
  Boards and Commissions with the Newly Established Council Districts and
  Establishing Policies and Procedures Regarding the Eligibility, Term and
  Nomination of Its Members.

  Presented a memo to the City Clerk’s Office requesting to add an item to the
  agenda to align the Commissions to the Council Districts.

  Spent some time in the Detective Bureau and saw the work behind the scenes that
  is done by the detectives. Thanked the Chief and the Detectives for the
  opportunity.

  Mayor Ancona would like to not get ahead of the game and allow the new members
  to make these decisions.

18D.  Councilwoman Martinez Muela

  18D.1 Discussion Regarding Plans to Transition to Seven Council Members
  Including Dais Upgrades and Other Potential Expenditures.

  The City should be taking a look at the budget now that the City Council is
  expanding. How will the dais work now that it will be going from five (5) members
  to seven (7) members.

  Would like staff recommendation and budget for the additional changes that will
  take place.

  Dr. Morales would like to get clarification regarding the budget component. Is it
  the budget for the changes or does it also include the stipends.

  18D.2 Update and Action Regarding the 4th of July Firework Activity.

  Requested update from Chief Lowry regarding the 4th of July firework activity.

  Chief Lowry provided an update. There was a 36 percent decrease in fireworks
  calls and priority calls dropped.

  10
   City Council Meeting Minutes of August 2, 2022

  Would like to see if the Council is interested in a presentation on banning fireworks
  from the City.

  Dr. Morales would like staff to include the enforcement mechanism if the City were
  to ban fireworks.

  18D.3 Discussion Regarding City Manager Spending Authority and Accountability
  of Expenditures to Council. Recommend Monthly Report to the Council.

  Request that the City Council receive a monthly report on the City Manager’s
  expenditures.

  City Manager would like clarification on how the information would be presented.

  Dr. Morales can column descriptor be added to the information already being
  provided on the warrant list.

18E.  Councilwoman Dr. Morales

  18E.1 Discussion and Action Regarding an Ordinance on Street Racing.

  18E.2 Discussion and Action Regarding Broadband and Digital Divide.

  Deputy Director Jason Mikaelian provided an update regarding the Broadband and
  Digital Divide. A final draft will be finalized by staff in August, and it will then be
  presented to the City Council.

  18E.3 Discussion and Action Regarding Cannabis Revenue.

  Would like to find out if the City is receiving this tax revenue.

  The City Manager informed that the City has received the second quarter revenues
  and the City is incredibly happy. A report will be brought to the City Council a
  report as to what the revenues look like, what is being projected and what the
  revenue can be used for.

  18E.4 Discussion and Action Regarding Catalytical Converter Thefts.

  Community meetings have been held and the STOP program has been addressed.
  The community is providing feedback and it is the same, there is street racing
  occurring, folks who want to take over specific intersections, donuts on major
  intersections.

  Chief Lowry informed that the Vehicle Code already allows for individuals who are
  speeding to be arrested.

  Chief Lowry provided update regarding the catalytic converter thefts.
